data.updated: 22 September 2026 (evening — NO LEVEL, GEOGRAPHY OR REVISION-DATE CHANGE on any of the five markets. The evening tier-A sweep asserted complete: 17 SOURCES, EXIT 0, EVERY ONE LOGGED, NONE WRITTEN OFF AS UNREACHABLE. ONE BLIND SPOT CLOSED TONIGHT: ZANZIBAR'S MINISTRY OF HEALTH WAS READ DIRECTLY via its travel-advisory page, after two evenings of being declared unread. Travel Advisory No. 1 of 20 May 2026 is unrevised and operative: universal non-invasive thermal-scanner screening for all air and sea arrivals, plus a Traveller Surveillance Form (healthtravelznz.mohz.go.tz, online or paper) for anyone arriving from or transiting the DRC or Uganda. Tanzania still records zero Ebola cases. ALL FIVE ADVISORY SETS UNCHANGED. UK FCDO KENYA unchanged on its 4 September revision: against all travel to Mandera County, Tarbaj and Wajir East constituencies except Wajir Town, Wajir within 60km of the Somalia border, and Garissa County except Garissa Town, Lagdera and Balambala north and west of the Saka-to-C81 road; Nairobi and the main safari circuit unaffected. UK UGANDA unchanged, last substantive update 2 September recording WHO's late-August declaration that the Uganda outbreak is over plus the 28 August national-cleaning-day exemption; no part of Uganda under advise-against-travel. NOTE A DATE SPREAD WE HAVE NOT SETTLED: secondary sources variously give 25 and 27 August for the WHO declaration and 28 July for the Ugandan MoH declaration; we carry WHO certification 26 August and have not resolved it to a primary MoH notice. UK TANZANIA unchanged: all-but-essential within 20km of the Cabo Delgado border, heightened health screening for arrivals from Uganda and the DRC. UK RWANDA unchanged on its 4 September revision: DRC-Ebola border measures, the vape and e-cigarette ban, Reunion entry information, and the Gisenyi-Goma short-notice closure warning. CANADA unchanged on Kenya, last updated 9 September, exercise a high degree of caution, avoid all travel to Mandera, Wajir, Garissa and Lamu. GERMANY unchanged, last updated July 2026. FRANCE unchanged in substance on its 18 September revision and still the widest of the set: the Kenya-Somalia border zone formally deconseille TO 100KM INLAND, against the UK's 60km Wajir line. Its OCTOBER-DECEMBER clause is now effectively live: El Nino-accentuated short rains, flash flooding, landslides on road axes including urban, and a resurgence of cholera, typhoid and malaria. Kenya eTA via etakenya.go.ke unchanged. CANADA'S EBOLA BORDER MEASURES STILL EXPIRE 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 AT 23:59 EDT — SIX DAYS OUT TONIGHT, down from seven last night. The operative instrument remains the 30-day extension announced in August: foreign nationals who visited the DRC in the previous 21 days barred from entry, airlines barred from carrying them, and immigration documents suspended for applicants listing an affected country as last country of residence. NO successor or further-extension notice published as at this evening. P198 STAYS OPEN. The US CDC order (91 FR 58673-58679) still expires 4:59pm EDT 11 October 2026. RWANDA ENTRY RULE unchanged and still the strictest in the region: the MoH Notice on Enhanced Ebola Prevention Measures of 22 May 2026 is unrevised with NO announced end date — all foreign nationals who travelled to or transited the DRC within 30 days prior to intended travel are DENIED ENTRY, Rwandan nationals and foreign residents with valid proof of residency exempt; reinforced screening at land points of entry and enhanced entry controls at Kigali International. No September 2026 MoH statement published. The Rwanda-DRC border remains open. WHO's DON617 position that WHO 'advises against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries' still runs against Rwanda's bar, Canada's bar and the US order. HEALTH — WHO SITUATIONS HUB FETCHED AND READ DIRECTLY TONIGHT: THERE IS NO NEW DISEASE OUTBREAK NEWS SINCE DON617 OF 10 SEPTEMBER. DON617 therefore remains the CONFIRMED FLOOR: 6,757 confirmed cases and 3,267 deaths to 7 September, CFR 48.3%, 61 health zones across six provinces, Ituri the epicentre at 5,406 cumulative and North Kivu carrying the highest CFR at 65.4%. Most recent WHO items on the hub are the IHR Emergency Committee second-meeting report of 28 August, its temporary recommendations of 24 August, emergency guidance on the licensed Ebola vaccine in Bundibugyo outbreaks published 1 September, and Rapid Risk Assessment v4 of 20 August. HIGHER FIGURES ARE CIRCULATING AND ARE GRADED REPORTED, NOT CONFIRMED: 7,672 confirmed cases and 3,699 deaths to 20 September, CFR 48.2%, a day-on-day move of +58 cases and +23 deaths split Ituri 38, North Kivu 14, Haut-Uele 5 and Tshopo 1 (Outbreak News Today, 20 September 2026, citing DRC MoH). We did not re-fetch a primary document for those. UGANDA: outbreak closed, 20 confirmed cases, last confirmed case discharged 16 June 2026; screening maintained at 22 points of entry plus Entebbe International, Mulago Ebola treatment centre on standby, PHEOC on alert. BLIND SPOTS DECLARED: Africa CDC's posted Epidemic Intelligence Weekly is STILL THE AUGUST 2026 EDITION for the third consecutive evening — no September bulletin on the main index or on the Africa Health Knowledge Hub, two queries run; the source is reachable, the bulletin simply is not out. KCAA's e-AIP AIC index was read directly and carries no dated circular in window. TANAPA and NCAA tariff pages show no new notice. A UGANDAN BLIND SPOT PARTLY CLOSES: UWA's own Rates/Tariffs page (read directly, page last modified 3 March 2026) DOES publish a 'Tariff changes 2026-2027' document, contrary to our standing note that only trade sources carried a replacement for the lapsed July 2024-June 2026 conservation tariff. The page is internally inconsistent — it still links the EXPIRED tariff as its main download and the tariff card still points at the 2022-2024 PDF. The 2026-2027 PDF was NOT parsed tonight, so NO Ugandan fee figure is changed or newly asserted.)

us.note: Terrorism, crime, kidnapping, unrest, health and 'Other'. Country level unchanged at 2. Re-issued 28 July 2026 (rendered page carries 'Date issued: July 28, 2026', verified 12 Aug 2026) — the 'Other (O)' indicator was added and the Nairobi neighbourhoods of EASTLEIGH and KIBERA are now LEVEL 4 DO NOT TRAVEL (crime, kidnapping), corrected from our earlier Level 3 reading. Also Level 4: Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu, Tana River (except Tsavo NP), Kilifi north of the C103 and coastal areas north of Malindi; West Pokot and western Turkana; Marsabit and Turkana within 50km of Ethiopia. Nairobi hotel corridors (Westlands, Upper Hill, Gigiri, CBD, Karen), Diani and Watamu are not in any Level 4 area.

uk.note: Against travel to the Kenya–Somalia border and parts of Lamu/north coast; core safari & coast areas unaffected. HEALTH LAYER (separate from the advisory): three G7 governments now carry a dengue notice on Kenya naming the COAST — US Embassy Nairobi health alert 3 Aug 2026 (coast, Wajir, Garissa); Germany 3 Aug 2026; CANADA added Kenya to Travel Health Notice 517 on 8 Sep 2026. Canada’s notice is Level 1 — practise health precautions — and did NOT change any country risk level. Kenya MoH: 1,678 dengue cases and 5 suspected deaths in Garissa and Wajir as at 26 Aug 2026 (1,276 in Dadaab), PHEOC activated; separately Mombasa recorded 3,989 cases Jan–May 2026 (Health CS Aden Duale via The Standard). The UK has NOT added a dengue line to its Kenya health page as at 9 Sep 2026.

us.note: Do not travel — VERIFIED against travel.state.gov 3 Sep 2026. Date issued 4 June 2026; indicators Crime, Health, Terrorism, Unrest. Advisory history states Uganda was raised from Level 3 to Level 4 on 17 May 2026 'due to the Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease outbreak in Ituri Province in the DRC'. The page still describes Kampala mass-gathering restrictions, 21-day quarantine for DRC arrivals and the DRC border closure. NOT UPDATED since 4 June — 91 days — despite Uganda MoH declaring the outbreak over on 28 Jul 2026 and WHO certifying the end on 26 Aug 2026. State's own text links to a CDC travel health notice filed under a Level 2 path. Divergence with the UK (Level 1) is now two full levels.

uk.note: CORRECTED 28 Aug 2026 — the UK advises against travel to NO part of Uganda. We carried 'against all-but-essential travel to Queen Elizabeth & Semuliki NP' for nine months after the FCDO lifted it on 2 December 2025. Verified against gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/uganda and its Regional risks page, 28 Aug 2026: still current at 25 Aug 2026, updated 27 Jul 2026, and the Warnings page carries no advice-against-travel block at all. Every 'advises against all travel' line on the Regional risks page refers to the DRC and South Sudan, NOT Uganda. Western Uganda carries caution language only (ADF, Kasese/Bundibugyo attacks Nov 2025). Bwindi and Mgahinga are open; armed escort on gorilla tracking is described as routine practice, not a warning. NOTE: mandatory National Cleaning Day, final Saturday monthly 07:00-10:00, nationwide movement restriction — tourists exempt (Uganda Police, 24 Aug 2026).

us.note: Reconsider travel — RAISED from Level 2 to 3 on 31 Oct 2025 ('unrest' indicator added). Grounds: unrest, crime, terrorism (highest risk in the Mtwara Region near the Mozambique border), and targeting of gay & lesbian individuals. Verified vs travel.state.gov 4 Aug 2026.

uk.note: No advisory against travel except within 20km of the Mozambique (Cabo Delgado) border.

us.note: As mainland Tanzania (Level 3 since 31 Oct 2025); no Zanzibar-specific carve-out. Verified 4 Aug 2026.
Reconsider travel — regional Ebola risk and DRC border security.

uk.note: CORRECTED 8 Sep 2026 — the FCDO advice-against area is PARTS OF RUSIZI DISTRICT ONLY: the parts within 10km of the DRC border, including the Rwandan islands in Lake Kivu and Kamembe Airport. RUBAVU IS NOT NAMED. We carried 'Rubavu, Rusizi' and were overstating it — Gisenyi/Rubavu on Lake Kivu carries no advice against travel, and Kigali, Musanze/Volcanoes, Nyungwe and Akagera are all outside the advice-against area. Verified by reading gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/rwanda/entry-requirements directly on 8 Sep 2026; the page's own public-updated-at is 4 Sep 2026 10:15 BST. ENTRY RULE, separate from the advisory: Rwanda denies entry to any foreign national who has travelled to or transited through the DRC in the 30 days before travel, and runs enhanced screening at Kigali International Airport and DRC land crossings (Rwanda MoH notice, 22 May 2026; FCDO links to RBC for it). Commonwealth citizens get a free 30-day visa on arrival.
